'''Eva Zažímalová''' (born 18 February 1955) is a [[Czech Republic|Czech]] [[biochemist]] and from March 2017 to March 2025 the president of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="cas">{{cite web|title=Professor Eva Zažímalová has been appointed President of the Czech Academy of Sciences for the period 2017–2021 - Akademie věd České republiky|url=http://www.avcr.cz/en/media/news-archive/Professor-Eva-Zazimalova-has-been-appointed-President-of-the-Czech-Academy-of-Sciences-for-the-period-20172021/|website=www.avcr.cz|publisher=Czech Academy of Sciences|accessdate=27 March 2017|language=en|archive-date=28 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328105634/http://www.avcr.cz/en/media/news-archive/Professor-Eva-Zazimalova-has-been-appointed-President-of-the-Czech-Academy-of-Sciences-for-the-period-20172021/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Between 2020 and 2025, Zažimalová served as a [[Scientific Advice Mechanism|Chief Scientific Advisor to the European Commission]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Members of the Group of Chief Scientific Advisors |url=https://scientificadvice.eu/about-us/group-of-chief-scientific-advisors/about-the-advisors/|publisher=Scientific Advice Mechanism to the European Commission |access-date=16 May 2025}}</ref>

She studied [[biochemistry]] at the Faculty of Science of [[Charles University]] in Prague in 1974–1979. Since 1983, she has worked in the Institute of Experimental Botany of the Czech Academy of Sciences. Between 2003 and 2007, she was the deputy director of this institute, from 2007 to 2012 she led the institute as its director. At Charles University, Eva Zažímalová was habilitated in 2004 and in 2013 she was appointed professor of plant anatomy and physiology.<ref name="cas"/> She was elected to the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts]],<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.avcr.cz/en/about-us/cas-structure/academy-council/list-of-members-of-academy-council/prof.-rndr.-eva-zazimalova-csc./ |title = Prof. RNDR. Eva Zažímalová, CSC. - Akademie věd České republiky}}</ref> and is a [[member of the Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Za%C5%BE%C3%ADmalov%C3%A1_Eva|title=Academy of Europe: Zažímalová Eva|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

She has devoted herself to the molecular mechanisms of the effect of [[plant hormone]]s. Her research work is focused predominantly on the phytohormone [[auxin]], its metabolism and the molecular mechanisms of its activity and transport in plant cells. The results of her research have found applications for instance in agriculture.<ref name="cas"/>
